transcript:
Meeting header:
Title: Legal & Finance: MSA/DPA, SLA & Pricing Clearance - Northbay Health
Date: 2026-04-01
Start: 16:30 UTC | Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Lena Patel (Redwood AE); Marcus O'Neill (Redwood SE); Chen Wu (Redwood CSM); Aisha Rahman (Northbay Procurement); Devon Hayes (Northbay Legal); Ravi Srinivasan (Northbay Cloud); Marta Lopez (Northbay Finance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Discussion of MSA/DPA redlines, SOC2 evidence, KMS and SSO integration, billing cadence, and SLA windows for pilot.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlines/pricing; SE to validate KMS path; customer to schedule internal approval meeting.

Topics: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA SLOs & credits, pricing bands for pilot vs dedicated, KMS/HSM options, SSO/SAML, audit logs retention, PO & billing cadence, vendor committee review timeline.

Questions noted:
- "Can your Private deployment support our HSM-backed keys?"
- "Is there an emergency rollback SLA for model degradation?"
- "How will billing show burst vs committed usage?"

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Patel: okay hey everybody thanks for joining um we're expecting about an hour so i'll kick us off briefly. welcome northbay team. quick intro from redwood side, marcus (se), chen (csm) — and then we'd love quick intros from your side.
[00:12] Aisha Rahman: hi it's Aisha, procurement. we'll be handling the vendor intake side, and we've got devon from legal, ravi who's our cloud lead and marta covering finance.
[00:20] Marcus O'Neill: great, nice to meet you all. just to set expectations — today's goal is to clear the MSA/DPA signoffs, confirm KMS/SSO constraints, and align on final pilot pricing.
[00:35] Devon Hayes: right, um we did a pass on the DPA — couple of asks: stronger audit log guarantees, data residency language for EU telemetry, and a KMS/bring-your-own-key option.
[00:46] Lena Patel: noted. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments, and we have an HSM integration in our on-prem package. i'll let marcus walk through technical limitations though.
[00:57] Marcus O'Neill: yeah so, quick technical note — for hosted API we offer envelope encryption with customer keys in our KMS integration, but for full HSM-backed keys we generally route to our Private VPC or on-prem appliance. there is a nuance on tokenization and kv cache encryption that i can detail.
[01:15] Ravi Srinivasan: sorry to interrupt, when you say "route to Private" — does that require a full Private deployment or is there a hybrid where only key ops are isolated?
[01:22] Marcus O'Neill: good question. we have a hybrid mode in beta where key material is kept in your KMS and calls still go to hosted inference endpoints, but that path has a slightly higher latency profile and is dependent on key roundtrip times. i'll add latency numbers in the follow-up.
[03:20] Marta Lopez: on billing — we need to understand how burst charges show up, and can we get an invoicing cadence monthly vs quarterly — our AP team favors monthly. also any minimum commitment for pilot?
[03:35] Lena Patel: for pilots there's no long-term minimum; for dedicated we discuss reserved capacity commitments. pricing sheet i'll share has both pilot band and dedicated commit options. monthly invoicing is fine; we can include optional billing sync to your PO system.
[05:10] Devon Hayes: on SLA — what uptime SLOs do you commit for the pilot vs production? and what's the credit remedy?
[05:22] Marcus O'Neill: hosted API SLA for production is our standard 99.9% for request availability; pilot programs we often set expectations lower — we can commit to 99.5 during pilot but provide compensation in service credits if there's sustained outages. the MSA includes the exact credit formula.
[07:40] Aisha Rahman: are there export controls or data residency limitations we should be aware of? we have EU patient data workflows.
[07:54] Lena Patel: yes, we support regional routing — you can pin requests to eu-west endpoints and have data residency controls in the DPA. we also have an export-controls questionnaire for regulated data — i'll attach in the follow-up.
[12:10] Devon Hayes: on DPA changes: we've highlighted three high-level edits — audit log retention to 7 years, right to audit clause phrasing, and breach notification timelines. can you accept 72 hours breach notification?
[12:30] Marcus O'Neill: 72 hours is tight but that's industry standard; we can accept notification within 72 hours for confirmed breaches, with an initial notification within 24 hours for suspected incidents. we'll capture that in the redline.
[18:05] Marta Lopez: also we need a clear cost estimate for egress and data transfer fees, especially if we run large embeddings workloads.
[18:22] Lena Patel: yes, embeddings and large batch inference can have different egress profiles. pricing sheet will separate token charges, embedding unit pricing, and any data transfer / egress buckets. we'll call out estimates for a 1M token/month pilot.
[22:45] Ravi Srinivasan: technical deep dive — for the KMS integration, we need the integration pattern: do you call our KMS synchronously per request or is there envelope/key caching?
[23:00] Marcus O'Neill: we use envelope keys and have a short-lived cache of the decrypted key material in the runtime for performance; for strict compliance customers we can disable caching, but that will increase latency and costs. i'll show the cache TTL and perf impact numbers in the PoC.
[28:10] Devon Hayes: do you provide SOC2/ISO evidence and penetration test reports? we need to present them to our security committee.
[28:22] Chen Wu: yes — we publish SOC2 type II report artifacts under NDA. we can provide a SOC2 pack and most recent pentest summary; full reports go through our security sharing workflow. link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2 (requires NDA).
[34:00] Aisha Rahman: timeline-wise, we have a vendor committee meeting week of 2026-04-13. to get on that agenda we'd need vendor docs and pricing by 2026-04-06. can you meet that?
[34:15] Lena Patel: yes we can, we'll target sending redlines, pricing, and SOC2 pointer by 2026-04-03 to give you a few days to review.
[39:05] Devon Hayes: a couple more legal nitpicks — indemnity carveouts for third-party generated hallucinations, and we want explicit data deletion confirmation on contract termination.
[39:22] Marcus O'Neill: we have standard indemnity language and a model usage carveout; for data deletion we offer documented deletion flows and can provide a certificate of deletion for Private deployments. i'll get the clause references in the redline.
[45:30] Marta Lopez: about PO and billing — do you accept vendor forms or do we need Redwood's invoice template? also any net-45 vs net-30 flexibility?
[45:42] Lena Patel: we accept customer PO templates in most cases; payment terms are negotiable but standard is net-30 for pilot invoices. we can accept net-45 with pre-approval from finance for enterprise deals.
[50:10] Aisha Rahman: what competitors should we expect to see in procurement reviews? our team mentioned Anthropic, an internal build, and potentially an AWS-managed endpoint.
[50:20] Lena Patel: okay that's expected. we find procurement cares about price predictability, SOC2 evidence, and rollback paths. we'll highlight those in the packet.
[53:50] Devon Hayes: final ask — i'll send the DPA redline annotated. expect that by end of day 2026-04-02. once you get it, can you flag any non-starters quickly?
[54:05] Lena Patel: absolutely. we'll triage within 48 hours of receiving. marcus will review tech constraints, and chen will provide SOC2/pentest artifacts under NDA.
[54:30] Lena Patel: recap of next steps: redwood sends pricing + MSA/DPA redline examples + SOC2 link by 2026-04-03; SE runs KMS PoC and shares notes by 2026-04-10; northbay schedules vendor committee and confirms PO template by 2026-04-06.
[54:50] Aisha Rahman: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity. we'll follow up if committee date changes.
[55:05] Lena Patel: thanks all, we'll close out there. bye.

References shared in call:
- Pricing sheet (link in follow-up): Redwood pricing pilot vs dedicated (will attach)
- SOC2 & pentest pack (link requires NDA): https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2
- KMS/SSO integration checklist (to be shared by Marcus)

End of transcript.
